A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IBG/IBG-NN research. All 44 pages of v1 and 49 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable, and the text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original IBG-NN and IbgE results for node classification, traffic forecasting, knowledge graph completion, and synthetic efficiency experiments, including Tables 1–4 and Appendix L.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional adjacency-entry sampling, approximation-quality, sparsity, and memory experiments in Section 6 and Appendix M.

M1.justification: v2 adds diode-sampling SGD, which samples individual adjacency entries according to their weights and constructs a corresponding sampled loss (Appendix H.2). This substantially extends the optimization procedures beyond v1's node-sampling SGD. The underlying IBG factorization and main IBG-NN architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The real-world benchmark datasets and application domains are retained. v2 adds variable-density ER graph scenarios and Squirrel evaluations with progressively removed edges, including a no-graph endpoint (Appendices M.3.2–M.3.3). These extend sparsity and input-availability coverage within existing domains.

E2.justification: GCN becomes an evaluated comparator for fitting and inference memory in Appendix M.4.2 and Figure 10; v1 had no corresponding memory comparison. The comparator sets in the retained classification, forecasting, knowledge-graph, coarsening, and runtime experiments remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v1's large-graph experiment uses node sampling with ratio M/N. Its protocol is retained in v2 Appendix M.1.4, while v2 Section 6.3 reports adjacency-entry sampling with ratio M/N². v2 also introduces approximation-error measurements, controlled sparsity sweeps, and a three-layer, 128-feature memory comparison. Equal nominal sampling ratios therefore do not establish equivalent settings across the two samplers.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained community-count accuracy and Arxiv-Year densification sweeps, v2 tests approximation error versus community count, approximation stability across graph densities, classification under edge removal, and fitting versus inference memory (Figures 5, 7, 8, and 10). It also discusses the two sampling variants together. These substantially broaden analysis of the central approximation and scalability arguments.

E5.justification: The retained experiments use the same ten data splits or five seeds and mean/standard-deviation reporting. No increased run counts, new confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests are specified. Additional shaded plots and fitted curves do not introduce a new reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds diode-sampling results in Table 1 while preserving v1's node-sampling scores in Table 5; these are different protocols, not same-setting performance improvements. Figures 5, 7, 8, and 10 add approximation, sparsity, and memory outcomes. Table 2 corrects GloGNN's Chameleon accuracy from 771.21 to 71.21, and the FaberNet runtime points and fitted curves change from v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 9.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition H.1 and its diode-SGD proof, and substantially revises the former node-SGD analysis, including normalization, N-dependent factors, probability constants, and assumptions. The regularity bounds replace δ/(1+δ) with δ throughout Theorem 4.1 and related appendices. Equation (31)'s SVD initialization bound also changes its prefactor from N²/E to N/√E. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the central claims remain a densifying regularity lemma with rank independent of graph size and sparsity, directed IBG representations, O(N) neural processing, and strong performance across the same application domains. The additional evidence does not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds a limitation for tasks dependent on small local structures, while retaining the cross-graph transfer limitation. It adds proposed explanations involving directionality, global versus local interactions, and knowledge-graph expressiveness. Appendix J also distinguishes the two approximation metrics explicitly and corrects its description of approximation error as computational complexity.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses dataset-specific Γ values in Tables 10–12 and relabels κ as β/α in the hyperparameter tables. It documents handling community counts not divisible by four during initialization and changes the code-access link from GitHub to anonymous hosting. These are documentation/access changes; the PDFs do not establish changed settings for the retained experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cooperative Graph Neural Networks to the directed-graph related work and makes limited refinements to its distinctions from ICG and PieClam. PieClam's preprint-to-publication update refers to the same work. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the exposition: fitting is integrated into Section 4, initialization and sampling details are moved into reorganized appendices, and the complexity comparison moves into Appendix K. The main narrative is condensed and rewritten, while the experimental appendix gains a structured hierarchy separating domains, community count, densification, and efficiency.

P2.justification: v2 adds four analytical figures and separately displays the retained node-sampling comparison as Table 5. It redraws the FaberNet runtime panel, simplifies Table 1's header structure, expands hyperparameter tables, and relocates several existing displays. Most earlier plots are preserved, so their moves alone are not new results.

improvement.justification: Explicit Γ settings, corrected mathematical and numerical reporting, additional sparsity/memory checks, and the local-structure limitation make the retained contribution easier to assess. The net gain is limited: the new diode-SGD derivation has inconsistent normalization across Appendices H.2–H.3, and the new cut-similarity experiments leave their numerical estimation procedure unspecified. These gaps temper the evidential value of the substantial expansion.
